# Dashboard run comparison view (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

This epic delivers the core experiment comparison capability in the Dashboard:
data scientists can select two or more training or pipeline runs and view their
parameters and metrics side by side in a single comparison view, replacing the
current export-to-spreadsheet workflow. When exactly two runs are compared, the
view highlights which parameters and metrics changed between them (diff
presentation of the same comparison surface).

## Scope

- Multi-run selection from the existing runs list in the Dashboard (two or more
  training and/or pipeline runs).
- A comparison view presenting the selected runs' parameters and metrics side
  by side.
- Diff presentation for two selected runs: parameters and metrics that differ
  between the two runs are visually highlighted.
- Comparison reads run parameters and metrics from the same sources that back
  the existing per-run pages; no new backend data store is introduced.
- Out of scope: automatic best-run selection or promotion, comparison across
  clusters or across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can select two or more runs from the runs list in the Dashboard.
- For the selected runs, all recorded parameters and metrics are displayed side
  by side in a single comparison view.
- When exactly two runs are compared, parameters and metrics whose values
  differ between the two runs are highlighted as changed.
- The comparison view renders correctly for both training runs and pipeline
  runs, including runs that have partially missing parameters or metrics
  (handled gracefully, not dropped from the comparison).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics
  side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1): run diff view highlighting which parameters and metrics changed
  between two selected runs — consolidated with HLR-1 as a presentation mode of
  the same comparison surface, covered by this epic at the higher priority.

# Run linkage on registered model versions

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry side of run traceability: a registered
model version records a reference to the run that produced it, so downstream
consumers (such as the Dashboard registry UI) can resolve the producing run and
open a comparison. The Model Registry's custom properties on model versions are
the documented extension point for attaching this structured metadata.

## Scope

- Define and record a run reference on registered model versions using the
  model version metadata extension point (custom properties), identifying the
  training or pipeline run that produced the version.
- Make the run reference retrievable through the Model Registry REST API
  (OpenAPI-specified) as part of model version metadata.
- Preserve backward compatibility: existing model versions without a run
  reference remain valid and fully functional.
- Out of scope: automatic best-run selection or promotion, cross-cluster or
  cross-project linkage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A registered model version can carry a reference to the run that produced it,
  recorded through the model version metadata extension point.
- The run reference is retrievable via the Model Registry REST API for any
  model version that has one.
- Model versions registered before this change (no run reference) continue to
  be readable and manageable without migration.
- Registration flows that do not know their producing run succeed without a run
  reference (the field is optional).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, Model Registry portion): registered model versions link back to
  the run that produced them.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry UI

## Description

This epic delivers the Dashboard-side entry point for run comparison from the
Model Registry: from a registered model version page in the Dashboard, a user
can open a comparison of the run that produced it. It consumes the run
reference recorded on model versions by the Model Registry and the run
comparison capability delivered for the runs list, wiring them together in the
registry UI.

## Scope

- Add an action on the registered model version page in the Dashboard that
  opens a run comparison for the linked producing run.
- Resolve the run reference from model version metadata via the Model Registry
  REST API.
- Handle model versions that have no run reference gracefully (action hidden or
  disabled with an explanatory state).
- Out of scope: comparison across clusters or projects; promotion workflows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- From a registered model version page in the Dashboard that has a run
  reference, a user can open a comparison view of the linked run.
- The opened comparison presents the linked run's parameters and metrics using
  the same comparison surface available from the runs list.
- Model versions without a run reference do not present a broken entry point.
- The entry point works for both training and pipeline run references.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, Dashboard portion): a comparison can be opened from the Model
  Registry.

# Validate Data Science Pipelines run metadata in run comparison

## Description

This epic validates that Data Science Pipelines run metadata — the parameters
and metrics recorded on pipeline runs — renders correctly in the new run
comparison capability, from the perspective of the team that owns Data Science
Pipelines. Data Science Pipelines requires no code change for run comparison
(its run data already surfaces on the Dashboard's per-run pages); this epic
confirms that assumption holds once comparison is in place and documents any
gaps found, with remediation notes for follow-up.

## Scope

- Exercise the run comparison view with Data Science Pipelines runs covering
  representative parameter and metric shapes (including runs with missing or
  partially populated parameters/metrics).
- Confirm pipeline run parameters and metrics are surfaced in the comparison
  identically to how they appear on the existing per-run pages.
- Document any incompatibilities or data gaps discovered in pipeline run
  metadata, with concrete remediation notes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists covering comparison of Data Science Pipelines
  runs, with a defined pass/fail outcome per checked scenario.
- Pipeline run parameters and metrics are confirmed to render in the comparison
  view correctly, or every discrepancy is documented with a remediation note.
- No Data Science Pipelines code change is required for the comparison to work,
  or the required change is documented as a follow-up with scope.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0, validation portion): side-by-side comparison of run parameters
  and metrics must work for pipeline runs.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic delivers user documentation for the run comparison workflow, covering
both entry paths: comparing runs from the runs list in the Dashboard and opening
a comparison from the Model Registry via a model version's run reference. It
documents what the shipped capability does, after implementation is complete.

## Scope

- New documentation topic(s) covering the comparison workflow:
  - Selecting two or more runs from the runs list and reading the side-by-side
    parameter and metric comparison.
  - Interpreting the diff highlighting between two selected runs.
  - Opening a comparison from a registered model version in the Model Registry.
- Screenshots and step-by-step procedures matching the shipped UI.
- Cross-references from existing runs-list and Model Registry documentation.
- Out of scope: documentation of automatic best-run selection or promotion (out
  of scope for the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the runs
  list, including multi-run selection and the diff view for two runs.
- Published documentation covers opening a comparison from the Model Registry
  via a model version's run reference.
- All documented steps and screenshots match the implemented behavior — the
  content is technically reviewed against the implementation before publish.
- Documentation uses the standard Red Hat docs content process and tooling.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the registry.
